tasks.title: debugging code
tasks.tip: Paste the error and the function around it, and say what you expected instead. A shorter snippet is easier to check than a whole repo.
tasks.starter_prompt: Here is the error and the function. Explain the cause, then show the smallest change that fixes it.
tasks.caution: Do not paste private keys, customer data, or a private repository into a consumer chat that trains on chats by default.
tasks.measured: This page uses the coding board. It measures coding preference and software benchmarks, not your private codebase.

tasks.title: writing Excel formulas
tasks.tip: Name the columns and one example row. Ask for the formula and a sentence on what it assumes.
tasks.starter_prompt: Write an Excel formula for this table. Columns are named below. Explain the formula in one sentence.
tasks.caution: Do not paste a workbook of client or employee data into a consumer chat that trains on chats by default.
tasks.measured: The coding board is not an Excel exam. It is a proxy for formula and logic work, not spreadsheet layout.

tasks.title: writing SQL queries
tasks.tip: Include the table names and the question in plain language. Ask the model to name any assumption about the schema.
tasks.starter_prompt: Write a SQL query for this question. Use only the tables I listed, and say what the query assumes.
tasks.caution: Do not paste production rows or customer records into a consumer chat that trains on chats by default.
tasks.measured: The coding board measures code tasks, not your database or the correctness of a query against live data.

tasks.title: building a website
tasks.tip: Describe one page, the content, and what a visitor should do. Ask for a first version you can open, not a whole product.
tasks.starter_prompt: Build a single page for this purpose. Keep the copy short, and tell me how to open it locally.
tasks.caution: Do not put API keys or private customer content in the prompt if the chat trains on chats by default.
tasks.measured: The coding board measures coding tasks. It does not measure design taste or whether the page matches your brand.

tasks.title: writing a Python script
tasks.tip: Say the input, the output, and one example. Ask for a script you can run, plus how to run it.
tasks.starter_prompt: Write a Python script that does this job. Include a short example of how to run it.
tasks.caution: Do not include secrets or private files in the prompt if the chat trains on chats by default.
tasks.measured: The coding board measures coding work. It does not run the script on your machine.

tasks.title: reviewing a contract
tasks.tip: Ask for unusual clauses, missing terms, and questions to send back. It is a reading aid, not a lawyer.
tasks.starter_prompt: Read this contract. List unusual clauses, missing protections, and questions I should ask before signing.
tasks.caution: Do not paste a client contract into a consumer chat that trains on chats by default. Use a plan that does not train, or an open model you run yourself.
tasks.measured: The legal board measures legal reading benchmarks, not your contract and not legal advice.

tasks.title: summarizing a PDF
tasks.tip: Ask for the decision, the numbers that matter, and what the document does not say. Then check those points against the file.
tasks.starter_prompt: Summarize this document. Give the main decision, the important figures, and anything it leaves out.
tasks.caution: Do not upload a confidential PDF to a consumer chat that trains on chats by default.
tasks.measured: The legal board measures long-document reading, not whether a summary kept every page of your file.

tasks.title: summarizing a research paper
tasks.tip: Ask for the claim, the method, and the limit of the evidence. Do not treat the summary as a citation you can quote.
tasks.starter_prompt: Summarize this paper. State the claim, how it was tested, and the main limit of the evidence.
tasks.caution: Do not upload an unpublished manuscript to a consumer chat that trains on chats by default.
tasks.measured: The legal board measures long-document reading, not scientific correctness.

tasks.title: reviewing a lease
tasks.tip: Ask which clauses cost money, which restrict you, and which dates matter. Check the answers against the lease.
tasks.starter_prompt: Read this lease. List the clauses that cost money, the restrictions, and the dates I should not miss.
tasks.caution: Do not paste a signed lease with personal details into a consumer chat that trains on chats by default.
tasks.measured: The legal board measures legal reading, not landlord-tenant law in your city and not legal advice.

tasks.title: writing a cover letter
tasks.tip: Give the role, two pieces of your real experience, and the tone you want. Ask for a short letter, then edit the facts yourself.
tasks.starter_prompt: Write a short cover letter for this role. Use only the experience I listed, and keep the tone direct.
tasks.caution: Do not include a home address, phone number, or other private details you do not want stored in a chat that trains by default.
tasks.measured: The writing board measures creative writing preference, not whether a letter gets you the job.

tasks.title: writing a LinkedIn post
tasks.tip: Say the point in one sentence and who it is for. Ask for a short post you would actually publish, not a slogan list.
tasks.starter_prompt: Write a short LinkedIn post about this point, for this reader. No hashtag pile and no fake story.
tasks.caution: Do not include a client's name or private company numbers if the chat trains on chats by default.
tasks.measured: The writing board measures writing preference, not reach or engagement.

tasks.title: writing a blog post
tasks.tip: Give the reader, the point, and two facts you want kept. Ask for a draft you can edit, with the facts unchanged.
tasks.starter_prompt: Draft a blog post for this reader. Keep these facts exactly, and mark any sentence you added.
tasks.caution: Do not paste unpublished client work into a consumer chat that trains on chats by default.
tasks.measured: The writing board measures writing preference, not accuracy of the facts you did not supply.

tasks.title: writing a product description
tasks.tip: List what the product does and what it does not do. Ask for plain sentences a buyer can check.
tasks.starter_prompt: Write a product description from these facts. Do not add features I did not list.
tasks.caution: Do not include unreleased pricing or a partner's private brief if the chat trains on chats by default.
tasks.measured: The writing board measures writing preference, not whether the description is legally accurate.

tasks.title: analyzing a spreadsheet
tasks.tip: Paste a small sample and the question, not the whole file. Ask what the sample cannot tell you.
tasks.starter_prompt: Look at this sample table and answer the question. Say what you cannot tell from this sample.
tasks.caution: Do not paste a full spreadsheet of customer or employee data into a consumer chat that trains on chats by default.
tasks.measured: The reasoning board measures hard exams, not spreadsheet software and not a forecast of your business.

tasks.title: solving math homework
tasks.tip: Ask for the steps, then cover the answer and try the next problem yourself. A correct-looking step can still hide a mistake.
tasks.starter_prompt: Solve this problem and show each step. After that, give me a similar problem to try.
tasks.caution: A worked answer is not a grade. Check the steps before you submit it.
tasks.measured: The reasoning board measures exam-style problems, not your assignment and not partial credit.

tasks.title: sorting support tickets
tasks.tip: Give the categories you already use and a few example tickets. Ask for a label and a one-line reason, then spot-check.
tasks.starter_prompt: Label each ticket with one of these categories and a one-line reason. If it fits none, say so.
tasks.caution: Do not paste tickets that contain customer personal details into a consumer chat that trains on chats by default.
tasks.measured: The speed board measures how fast a model answers, not how well it sorts your tickets.

tasks.title: extracting data from invoices
tasks.tip: Ask for the fields you need, one invoice at a time, and check the amounts against the file.
tasks.starter_prompt: Extract the supplier, date, and total from this invoice. If a field is missing, say missing.
tasks.caution: Do not upload customer invoices to a consumer chat that trains on chats by default.
tasks.measured: The speed board measures output speed, not extraction accuracy.

tasks.title: summarizing meeting notes
tasks.tip: Paste notes or a transcript you already have. Ask for decisions, owners, and open questions. This does not listen to audio.
tasks.starter_prompt: Turn these notes into decisions, owners, and open questions. Do not add anything that is not in the notes.
tasks.caution: Do not paste a confidential meeting transcript into a consumer chat that trains on chats by default.
tasks.measured: The general board measures everyday chat. It does not transcribe audio and it does not know who was in the room.

tasks.title: explaining a concept for an exam
tasks.tip: Name the concept and what you already understand. Ask for a plain explanation and one check question.
tasks.starter_prompt: Explain this concept as if I have to use it on an exam tomorrow. Then ask me one question to check it.
tasks.caution: An explanation can be tidy and still wrong. Check it against your course notes.
tasks.measured: The general board measures everyday answers, not your syllabus.

tasks.title: planning a trip
tasks.tip: Give the city, the dates in words, and what you care about. Ask for a rough shape of the days, then check opening hours yourself.
tasks.starter_prompt: Sketch a trip for this place and these interests. Keep each day loose, and list what I should confirm.
tasks.caution: Do not treat hours, prices, or visa rules as current. Confirm them with the official source.
tasks.measured: The general board measures everyday chat, not live travel availability.

tasks.title: making a logo
tasks.tip: Describe the subject, the colors, and where the logo will be used. Ask for one clear version, not a sheet of options.
tasks.starter_prompt: Make one logo for this name and this use. Keep it simple enough to read at a small size.
tasks.caution: A generated logo can resemble an existing mark. Check it before you print or register it.
tasks.measured: The image board measures preference on generated pictures, not trademark clearance.

tasks.title: making a product photo
tasks.tip: Name the product, the background, and the angle. Ask for one photo a shopper could understand.
tasks.starter_prompt: Make one product photo of this item on a plain background. Keep the shape accurate.
tasks.caution: Do not present a generated photo as a picture of a product you have not made.
tasks.measured: The image board measures picture preference, not whether the photo matches a physical product.

tasks.title: making a thumbnail
tasks.tip: Say the subject and the few words that must be readable. Ask for one thumbnail, not a poster.
tasks.starter_prompt: Make one thumbnail for this topic. Leave the title readable and the subject large.
tasks.caution: Do not imply a person said or did something they did not.
tasks.measured: The image board measures picture preference, not click rate.

tasks.title: editing a photo
tasks.tip: Say what must stay the same and what should change. Ask for one edit.
tasks.starter_prompt: Edit this photo as described. Change only what I named, and leave the rest alone.
tasks.caution: Do not edit a photo of a real person into something they did not do.
tasks.measured: The image board is mostly text-to-image. It is a weak proxy for editing an existing photo.

tasks.title: making a short ad
tasks.tip: Give the product, the one point, and the length in words. Ask for a single shot, not a campaign.
tasks.starter_prompt: Make a short ad clip for this product. Show the product and one reason to care.
tasks.caution: Do not invent a claim about price, health, or a customer result.
tasks.measured: The video board measures short generated clips, not whether an ad converts.

tasks.title: animating an image
tasks.tip: Say which part should move and which part must stay still.
tasks.starter_prompt: Animate this still image. Move only what I named, and keep the rest stable.
tasks.caution: Do not animate a real person into an action they did not do.
tasks.measured: The video board measures generated clips. It is a weak proxy for animating one still image.

tasks.title: writing a research report
tasks.tip: Ask for the sources first, then the summary. Say what would change your mind.
tasks.starter_prompt: Research this question. List the sources, then the answer, then what is still uncertain.
tasks.caution: Open every source. A confident paragraph can cite a page that does not say that.
tasks.measured: The search board measures answers with web search, not a finished research paper.

tasks.title: fact-checking a claim
tasks.tip: Paste the claim and ask what would confirm it and what would refute it.
tasks.starter_prompt: Check this claim. Name a source that supports it, a source that disputes it, and what is still unknown.
tasks.caution: Do not treat the model's verdict as the last word. Read the sources.
tasks.measured: The search board measures search answers, not a formal fact-check.

tasks.title: writing an email
tasks.tip: Say who it is to, what you need, and the tone. Ask for one short email.
tasks.starter_prompt: Write one email to this person. Say what I need, and keep it short enough to answer.
tasks.caution: Do not invent a promise, a price, or a fact the other person can check.
tasks.measured: The writing board measures preference on prose, not whether the email gets a reply.

tasks.title: rewriting a resume
tasks.tip: Paste the role and the real jobs. Ask it to use only what you already did.
tasks.starter_prompt: Rewrite this resume for this role. Use only the experience I gave you, and do not add a skill.
tasks.caution: Do not let it invent a job, a degree, or a result.
tasks.measured: The writing board measures prose, not whether a resume passes a screen.

tasks.title: outlining a presentation
tasks.tip: Give the audience, the one point, and how long you have. Ask for an outline, not slides.
tasks.starter_prompt: Outline a presentation for this audience and this point. One idea per section.
tasks.caution: An outline is not a finished deck, and it can skip the objection your audience will raise.
tasks.measured: The writing board measures prose. It does not measure slides.

tasks.title: writing a video script
tasks.tip: Say the viewer, the point, and the length in words. Ask for a spoken script.
tasks.starter_prompt: Write a spoken script for this topic. Open with the point, then the steps, then what to do next.
tasks.caution: Do not invent a quote, a statistic, or a personal story.
tasks.measured: The writing board measures prose, not whether a video holds attention.

tasks.title: writing social captions
tasks.tip: Give the post, the audience, and the one action. Ask for a few captions, not a campaign.
tasks.starter_prompt: Write three captions for this post. Each one should ask for the same action.
tasks.caution: Do not invent a customer result, a price, or a review.
tasks.measured: The writing board measures prose, not reach.

tasks.title: translating a document
tasks.tip: Name the language and say which terms must stay exact. Ask for a translation, not a summary.
tasks.starter_prompt: Translate this into the language I named. Keep names and numbers as they are, and mark anything you are unsure of.
tasks.caution: Have a person check anything you would sign, file, or send to a customer.
tasks.measured: No board on this site measures translation. The general ranking is only a stand-in for clear writing.

tasks.title: making study flashcards
tasks.tip: Paste the notes and ask for a question on the front and a short answer on the back.
tasks.starter_prompt: Turn these notes into flashcards. One fact per card, and do not add a fact that is not in the notes.
tasks.caution: Check the cards against the source. A tidy card can still be wrong.
tasks.measured: The general board measures everyday answers, not whether a card matches your course.

tasks.title: comparing a loan
tasks.tip: Give the amount in words, the term, and what you would use it for. Ask what to compare, not which loan to take.
tasks.starter_prompt: List what to compare on these loans. Do not tell me which one to take.
tasks.caution: This is not financial advice. Confirm the terms with the lender.
tasks.measured: The general board does not measure lending decisions.

tasks.title: planning for retirement
tasks.tip: Say the age you want to stop working and what you already save. Ask for questions to take to an adviser.
tasks.starter_prompt: List the questions I should ask an adviser about retirement. Do not tell me what to buy.
tasks.caution: This is not financial advice. A chat does not know your taxes, debts, or accounts.
tasks.measured: The general board does not measure retirement planning.

tasks.title: checking a question about taxes
tasks.tip: Say the country and the year in words. Ask what to look up, not what you owe.
tasks.starter_prompt: Explain how to look this tax question up on the official site. Do not tell me what I owe.
tasks.caution: This is not tax advice. Use the revenue agency's own page or a tax preparer.
tasks.measured: The general board does not measure tax law.

tasks.title: explaining a mortgage
tasks.tip: Ask what the words mean. Do not ask which mortgage to sign.
tasks.starter_prompt: Explain these mortgage words in plain language, and list what I should ask the lender.
tasks.caution: This is not financial advice. The offer from the lender is the one that counts.
tasks.measured: The general board does not measure mortgage offers.

tasks.title: building a slide deck
tasks.tip: Say the audience and the one point. Ask for slides you can edit, not a picture of slides.
tasks.starter_prompt: Build a short slide deck for this audience and this point. One idea per slide.
tasks.caution: Check every claim before you present it.
tasks.measured: This task is not ranked. No board on this site measures presentation tools.

tasks.title: designing a poster
tasks.tip: Describe the subject, the few words that must be readable, and the size in words.
tasks.starter_prompt: Design one poster for this event. Keep the title readable and the subject large.
tasks.caution: Do not copy a poster, a logo, or a photo you do not have rights to use.
tasks.measured: This task is not ranked. Design tools are listed by what the app says it can do, not by a board.

tasks.title: making a voiceover
tasks.tip: Paste the script and say the pace. Ask for a read, not a new script.
tasks.starter_prompt: Read this script aloud at a calm pace. Do not change the words.
tasks.caution: Do not imitate a real person's voice without permission.
tasks.measured: This task is not ranked. No board on this site measures voice.
